near_duplicate_sentence_pairs.sentence_a: The low-humidity setting lets more air through.
near_duplicate_sentence_pairs.sentence_b: The high-humidity setting is more closed, so more moisture stays near the food.

point_one_role_text: Provide a practical sorting rule that replaces the misleading “fruit versus vegetable” shortcut: identify whether the food mainly risks wilting or mainly releases ethylene that can speed up nearby produce. Use ethylene-heavy items such as apples, pears, bananas, and tomatoes versus moisture-sensitive leafy greens and broccoli, while noting that strawberries and oranges are fruit exceptions that still favor high humidity.
point_two_role_text: Define the boundary of the crisper-drawer advice by showing that some familiar produce should not be routed into either humidity setting at all. Contrast tomatoes and bananas, which Iowa State identifies for counter storage, with potatoes, sweet potatoes, onions, and garlic, which need a cool, dry environment rather than being casually treated as counter-stored items.
